diagnosis_explanation: Syncope means fainting or passing out. It can happen when your body does not send enough blood to your brain. This can be caused by many things. It is important to understand why it happened.
medication_rationale:
Aspirin 81 mg:
This medicine helps prevent blood clots. Blood clots can cause problems with your heart or brain. You might not feel this medicine working. It is important for preventing future issues.

Multivitamin, Nephrocaps:
This medicine gives your body needed vitamins and minerals. It is especially important for your kidneys. You will not feel this medicine working directly. It helps your body stay healthy overall.

Fosrenol 500 mg:
This medicine helps your body get rid of extra phosphate. Too much phosphate can be harmful. You may notice it helps reduce stomach upset. Taking it with food is best. Call your doctor if you have bad constipation or stomach pain.

Lisinopril 2.5 mg:
This medicine helps your heart pump blood more easily. It can lower your blood pressure. You might feel less tired over time. Your blood pressure will likely go down. Call your doctor if you feel dizzy or get a bad cough.

Coreg 3.125 mg:
This medicine helps your heart beat slower and with more power. It can also lower your blood pressure. You may feel less tired or short of breath. Your heart will work better. Call your doctor if you feel very dizzy, tired, or have slow heartbeats.

Procrit 10,000 units:
This medicine helps your body make more red blood cells. Red blood cells carry oxygen through your body. You may feel more energy as it works. Your tiredness may decrease. Call your doctor if you have trouble breathing or chest pain.

Heparin 5000 units:
This medicine helps prevent blood clots. It is given under your skin. You might notice some bruising or redness where the shot is given. This is usually normal. Call your doctor if you notice any bleeding that is hard to stop.
recovery_trajectory:
**Week 1:**
- You may feel tired and a bit weak. This is normal.
- Take short walks inside your home.
- Rest when you feel tired.
- Eat your usual foods.
- Drink plenty of fluids unless told otherwise.
- Your goal is to walk a little more each day.
- Call your doctor if you feel like you might pass out again.

**Week 2:**
- Your energy levels might start to improve slowly.
- You can do light activities around the house.
- Avoid sudden movements or standing up too fast.
- Continue to drink plenty of fluids.
- Your goal is to walk to your mailbox and back.
- Call your doctor if you have new chest pain or shortness of breath.

**Week 3:**
- You may feel more like yourself this week.
- You can try short walks outside.
- Avoid very hot environments or standing for long periods.
- Keep drinking plenty of fluids.
- Your goal is to walk for 10 minutes at a time.
- Call your doctor if you have another episode of passing out.

**Week 4:**
- Most days should feel more comfortable than before.
- You can return to most normal daily activities.
- Listen to your body and rest when needed.
- Keep up with good hydration.
- Your goal is to walk for 15 minutes most days.
- Call your doctor if you have concerns about your recovery.

**When to expect improvement:**
- You should feel more steady over the next few weeks.
- Continue to avoid triggers that may have caused passing out.
- Slowly increase your activity as you feel stronger.
- Seek medical care if you feel faint again.
escalation_guide:
CALL 911 IMMEDIATELY
These symptoms are life-threatening. Do not drive yourself.
- Loss of consciousness or fainting: This can be a sign of a serious problem.
- Chest pain that does not go away: This can mean your heart is not getting enough blood.
- You cannot breathe or are breathing very fast: Your body is not getting enough oxygen.
- Sudden face drooping or arm weakness: These are signs of a stroke. Minutes matter.
- Uncontrolled bleeding that will not stop: This needs immediate medical care.
- Seizure: This is a medical emergency.

GO TO THE ER TODAY
Do not wait until tomorrow. Go within a few hours.
- Fever above 101 degrees F that will not come down: This can mean your body has an infection.
- Severe pain that medicine does not help: This needs urgent care.
- Significant swelling in one leg, especially with pain: This could be a blood clot.
- Confusion or disorientation, new and getting worse: This needs to be checked right away.
- Cannot keep fluids down for 12 hours or more: This can lead to bad dehydration.

CALL YOUR DOCTOR
Call during office hours. Do not go to the ER for these.
- Mild pain that is slowly improving: This is likely part of your recovery.
- Questions about a medicine or dose: Your doctor or nurse can help.
- Dizziness that is mild and improving: This can happen after fainting.
- Mild swelling without pain: This may be normal but should be checked.
